mechanism_narrative: When the FEDFUNDS rate rises by more than 0.25 percentage points over the next month, the S&P 500 anticipates higher future discount rates, leading to negative 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS increases by >0.25pp in the following month
failure_condition: In tightening regimes, 20-day forward returns are not statistically different from zero (p > 0.05) or FEDFUNDS rise <0.25pp in 80% of tightening episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in CPIAUCSL by at least 0.5% over two consecutive months predicts a disinflationary environment that supports S&P 500 gains in the following 60-day horizon.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL decreases by >=0.5% over two consecutive months
failure_condition: Over 60-day windows, returns are negative when CPIAUCSL declines by >=0.5% and positive otherwise, or the pattern fails to explain more than 10% of variance in 60-day returns.

mechanism_narrative: Rising PAYEMS (labor market strength) combined with UNRATE below 4% indicates a resilient labor market, which drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 days.
failure_condition: In >70% of similar labor-resilient episodes, 5-day forward returns are not positive or the combination of high PAYEMS and low UNRATE fails to precede positive returns.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in GDPC1 (goods orders) followed by a subsequent rise in HOUST (housing starts) over the next 20 days signals accelerating business and consumer demand, pushing S&P 500 forward returns to the positive.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 increases then HOUST increases within 10 trading days
failure_condition: No statistically significant positive 20-day returns when both proxies follow the described pattern in expansionary regimes (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly decline in INDPRO (industrial production) exceeding 2% while FEDFUNDS remains below 2% suggests supply-side weakness that depresses equity valuations, producing negative 60-day forward returns.
failure_condition: In >50% of supply-contraction months, 60-day returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.1).

mechanism_narrative: When UNRATE falls below 3% for three consecutive months, the S&P 500 anticipates a labor market loosening that supports higher corporate profits and positive 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: Over 40 such periods, 20-day returns are not positive (mean <= 0) or the effect is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A persistent drop in RSAFS (money supply growth) below -0.5% for two months indicates deflationary pressure, which typically precedes S&P 500 declines in the next 60-day window.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS decreases by >0.5% for two consecutive months
failure_condition: Deflationary episodes do not consistently produce negative 60-day SPX returns or the correlation falls below -0.2.

mechanism_narrative: Concurrent strength in PAYEMS and a sharp rise in HOUST (both over 10% change in a month) signals a labor market boom that fuels optimism and drives positive 5-day S&P 500 forward returns.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by >10% and HOUST increases by >10% in the same month
failure_condition: In 80% of similar labor-boom months, 5-day returns are not positive or the proxies move in opposite directions.
